classification.difficultyReason: Test a proposed parallelogram by solving one supplementary-angle condition and checking another for consistency.

content.prompt: Is this shape a parallelogram? Explain your reasoning.

spec.description: An unshaded slanted quadrilateral resembling a parallelogram, with approximately horizontal upper and lower sides, four interior angle arcs and no parallel markings.
spec.mathematics: Upper-left angle 110°, upper-right angle (25x − 5)°, lower-left angle 70°, lower-right angle (12x + 68)°. Illustration coordinates preserve the source appearance without asserting measured angles or parallelism.
spec.answerVisibility: All four supplied angle labels are permanent givens. No solved value or conclusion appears in the question diagram.

answer.short: No. A parallelogram would require $x=3$, but then another adjacent-angle pair sums to $174^{\circ}$ rather than $180^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
If the shape were a parallelogram, adjacent interior angles would be supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}110+(25x-5)&=180\\25x+105&=180\\25x&=75\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Check the lower adjacent-angle pair:
$$\begin{align*}70+(12x+68)&=70+12(3)+68\\&=174\ne180\end{align*}$$
These angles are not supplementary, so the shape is not a parallelogram.
